summary:
Session 2026-11-16.

Session 2026-11-16 (pre-open). 100% cash, no trades. Context: Huang has resigned from Nvidia; Treasury Sec. Bessent demands an external CEO and answers in 10 days on China/Singapore chip compliance. NVDA closed 162.85, about -3% pre-market, and reports 11/17 after close. AMD -8.75% Friday and -5% pre-market. QQQ -1.2% and SPY -0.6% pre-market. The 10y yield is 5.13% and the market prices a 100% chance of a December Fed hike. Examined: TU (+19% pre on an unsolicited Quebecor bid, already priced), CGON (+30% on a Phase 3 win, priced), SMMT (-15% on an FDA ivonescimab setback, priced), HELP (Phase 3 news, small cap), PERI (guidance withdrawn, deal pending, pinned). None offers an edge at the open. Next: after NVDA earnings on 11/17, look for a post-event entry in NVDA, semis or the beaten-down FTNT, INTC and NOW if a base forms. Watch the Bessent/Nvidia 10-day deadline, yields and the Fed.
notes:
Session 1 (2026-10-29): Stayed cash. Looked at GOOGL (-12% EPS miss/capex), NOW (-27%), FTNT (-20% despite beat/raise), ADT (take-private, pinned), CROX (+21% priced in).
Session 2 (10-30): Premarket tech selloff: INTC -25%, AMZN -6%, AMD -9%, DELL -8%. Cash.
Session 3 (11-02): SPY -1.77%, QQQ -3.47%, INTC -28.6%, RDDT -29%. Cash.
Session 4 (11-03): Falling knives kept falling: FTNT 126 (-7%), INTC 60 (-8.8%). Lesson: buying rebounds right after a crash would have lost; wait for stabilisation.
Sessions 5-6 (11-10, 11-11): Cash. Hot CPI, 10y near 5%, Fed hike bets. CRWV +24.7% on beat.
Session 7 (11-12): Cash. WSJ: Nvidia board weighed removing Huang. NVDA -8% pre.
Session 8 (11-13): Cash. NVDA closed 166, Huang exit headlines, House subpoena threat.
Session 9 (11-16): Cash. Huang has resigned; Bessent demands external CEO, answers in 10 days on China/Singapore chip compliance. NVDA 162.85 close, ~-3% pre, earnings 11/17 AMC. AMD -8.75% Fri, -5% pre. SPY -0.6% pre, QQQ -1.2%. 10y 5.13%, market prices 100% Dec Fed hike. TU +19% pre (Quebecor unsolicited non-binding bid - already priced), CGON +30% (Ph3 win - priced), SMMT -15% (FDA says ivonescimab not approvable as-is), PERI withdrew guidance (Affle deal pending, pinned). No trade.
Lessons: whipsaw tape: gap-ups (CRWV 11-11) reversed next day, so not chasing was right. Catalyst moves (biotech, M&A bids) are priced by the open - no edge for pre-open orders. Open ideas: post-overreaction rebounds once base forms (FTNT, INTC, NVDA after 11/17 earnings); semis momentum still negative; macro 10y ~5%, rate-hike regime hurts long-duration tech.

prompt:
Your universe is every eligible US stock. Your style is a few high-quality trades.

- Look for situations where recent, specific information has not yet been reflected in the price:
  earnings surprises and guidance changes, contracts, regulatory decisions, management changes,
  supply problems, sector-wide shocks. Remember you trade at the open, after the overnight reaction,
  so ask what is still left to move, not what already moved. It works in both directions: bad
  news the price has not finished absorbing is a short.
- Prefer clear catalysts you can verify over vague narratives. A strong case beats a busy portfolio.
  A handful of positions at most is the expected shape; holding mostly cash is fine when your
  research turns up nothing compelling.
- Size positions by conviction and by how much could go wrong. Set stops and targets you would
  actually stand behind.
- Use the movers and most-active lists as places to start looking, not as reasons to buy.
